subject: Renewal + Expansion: dedicated pool upgrade 16→32 GPUs — pricing & throughput guarantees
messages:

Cc: Kyle Barnes <kyle@archai.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal / dedicated pool: exploring 16→32 upgrade

Connor —

Hope you had a good weekend. Our renewal for the dedicated pool is coming up (contract ends July 31). After the last quarter's rollout we need to plan for a larger committed pool: we want to move from 16 GPUs to 32 GPUs starting at the next term.

Two immediate asks from my side:
- Can you share an updated committed-rate card for 32x H100-equivalent reserved capacity?
- We need firm, documented throughput expectations (baseline RPS and burst behavior) and any credits tied to missed targets.

Procurement (cc'd Kyle) will be handling the contract mechanics. We are aiming for a 12-month term but would like a step-up clause if utilization ramps slower than expected. Also open to discussing a short transition window where we can burst on demand while reserved capacity spins up.

Can you get us a proposal this week? We’d like to present it to our CFO on Friday.

Thanks,
Emma

Head of Platform — Nimbus Robotics

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal / dedicated pool: exploring 16→32 upgrade

Emma —

Thanks for the clear asks and the heads-up on timing. We can absolutely support a 16→32 committed upgrade and I’ve attached a concise proposal that covers:
- Per-GPU reserved hourly rate for the 32-GPU block (volume discount applied)
- Throughput SLOs (baseline and burst), measurement method, and credit table
- Transition options (2-week burst window + on-demand scaling)

High-level summary here so you can share with your CFO quickly:
- New reserved rate (32-GPU block, H100-equivalent): $2.40 / GPU-hour (billed hourly). This is a 13% effective discount vs the current 16-GPU per-GPU rate of $2.75/hr.
- Throughput commitment: 24k tokens/min sustained across the pool (measured at the token-level at our edge) with a 15% burst buffer for short spikes.
- SLA credits: 5% credit of monthly committed spend if sustained throughput < 90% of the commitment for a rolling 7-day period; escalated remediation and a 72-hour performance remediation plan for repeated misses.
- Transition: two-week free burst allowance (up to 40 GPU-equivalent peak) during the first month of the new term to reduce rollout risk.

I’ve included Soojin (pricing) to confirm the numbers and Marcus (SRE/throughput) to confirm measurement and enforcement specifics. Kyle — I added a templated step-up clause in the attachment that addresses underutilization and ramp schedules.

Attachment: Redwood-SLA-Proposal-v2.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: 32GPU-Ratecard-2027.xlsx (xlsx)

If that looks roughly aligned I can convert the proposal into a redline-ready contract for your legal/procurement.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Connor / Soojin —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifying points from Nimbus: 
1) The CFO wants a stronger throughput guarantee during business hours (PST 8:00–18:00). Can you split the SLO into Peak window / Off-peak with different credit tiers?
2) The step-up clause Kyle will sign off on, but we want a clear underutilization credit if we are below 60% of committed usage for any 30-day window in first quarter.
3) On the transition: the two-week free burst is good, but we’d like a brief canary period where 4 GPUs are pinned for testing before the full pool becomes active.

Kyle — similar to other renewals we’ll loop finance/legal on the redline once we have a firm rate and SLO table.

Emma

Subject: Procurement: contract term and utilization protections

Connor / Neha —

Procurement notes and asks: 
- We prefer a 12-month firm term with a 30-day notice for renewal.
- Include a step-up schedule: month 1–3: 16 GPUs billed, month 4–6: 24 GPUs billed, month 7+: 32 GPUs billed (with customer option to accelerate). Billing should be aligned to committed hourly counts rather than instantaneous peak.
- Underutilization protection: if average utilization < 60% of committed pool over any rolling 30-day window in Q1, we request a 20% invoice credit on the underutilized portion for that month.
- We also need clarity on termination for convenience and a short statement assuring data isolation in the dedicated pool.

Please add Neha (cc) to handle legal/contracting language. Once we have a redline I'll push internally.

Regards,
Kyle

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal / dedicated pool: exploring 16→32 upgrade

Team — forwarding the thread from Nimbus / Kyle. They want a 12-month term with a step-up billing schedule and a stronger peak-window SLO. Proposed commercial counters below (for internal review):

Proposed commercial counters (recommended):
- Keep the 32-GPU reserved rate at $2.40 / GPU-hour but accept the step-up billing schedule as a launch concession (month 1–3: billed at 16 GPU hours, month 4–6: 24 GPU hours, month 7+: 32 GPU hours). This preserves their cashflow while guaranteeing eventual commitment.
- Peak / Off-peak SLO split: Peak (PST 08:00–18:00) at 30k tokens/min; Off-peak at 18k tokens/min. Maintain 15% burst allowance for both. Credit triggers: if sustained throughput < 90% peak SLO for a rolling 7-day window during peak hours => 5% monthly credit; repeated failure triggers remediation plan.
- Underutilization protection: offer a softer credit than requested — 10% invoice credit on the underutilized portion if utilization < 60% on a rolling 30-day window, but only within the first 90 days. After 90 days standard utilization clauses apply.
- Transition mechanics: 4-GPU pinned canary for 72 hours pre-full-activation. 2-week free burst allowance (up to 40 GPU-equivalent peak) in first month.

Operational asks for Marcus/SRE: confirm we can enforce Peak-window SLO measurement and that the 15% burst allowance can be implemented without impacting other tenant SLAs. Marcus — can you confirm the enforcement/measurement wording so Neha can include it in the redline?
Soojin — confirm the commercial acceptability of the 10% underutilization credit and whether the $2.40/hr figure is fundable in quota forecasts.

If we agree I’ll prepare a redline reflecting these counters and send to Emma/Kyle. 

—Connor
